hints: Differentiate $y = x^3 - 2bx^2 + b^2 x$ to get $\frac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 - 4bx + b^2$.
Factorise $(3x - b)(x - b) = 0$ to find stationary points at $x = \frac{b}{3}$ and $x = b$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate the curve equation with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 - 4bx + b^2$$

Set the derivative equal to zero to find the stationary points:
$$3x^2 - 4bx + b^2 = 0 \implies (3x - b)(x - b) = 0$$
$$x = \frac{b}{3} \quad \text{or} \quad x = b$$

Since $a$ is the $x$-coordinate of the maximum point located to the left of the minimum point at $x = b$:
$$a = \frac{b}{3} \implies b = 3a$$

ai_rubric.Stationary Points and Curve Properties: Differentiates to $3x^2 - 4bx + b^2$ (B1). Factorises $(3x - b)(x - b) = 0$ (M1). Identifies $x = b/3$ (A1). Shows $b = 3a$ (A1).

skill_tags: Finding an Area Between a Line and a Curve

hints: Find $y_A = 4a^3$ and area of triangle under line $OA = \frac{1}{2}(a)(4a^3) = 2a^4$.
Integrate curve from $0$ to $a$: $\int_0^a (x^3 - 6ax^2 + 9a^2 x) dx = \frac{11}{4}a^4$.
Subtract triangle area to show shaded area $= \frac{3}{4}a^4$.
walkthrough:
Substitute $b = 3a$ into the curve equation:
$$y = x^3 - 2(3a)x^2 + (3a)^2 x = x^3 - 6ax^2 + 9a^2 x$$

Find the $y$-coordinate of point $A$ at $x = a$:
$$y_A = a^3 - 6a(a^2) + 9a^2(a) = a^3 - 6a^3 + 9a^3 = 4a^3 \implies A = (a, 4a^3)$$

Calculate the area under the straight line $OA$ from $x = 0$ to $x = a$ (area of right triangle):
$$\text{Area}_{\text{line}} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times a \times 4a^3 = 2a^4$$

Calculate the definite integral for the area under the curve from $x = 0$ to $x = a$:
$$\text{Area}_{\text{curve}} = \int_0^a (x^3 - 6ax^2 + 9a^2 x) dx = \left[ \frac{x^4}{4} - 2ax^3 + \frac{9a^2 x^2}{2} \right]_0^a$$
$$\text{Area}_{\text{curve}} = \frac{a^4}{4} - 2a(a^3) + \frac{9a^2(a^2)}{2} = \frac{a^4}{4} - 2a^4 + \frac{9a^4}{2} = \left(\frac{1 - 8 + 18}{4}\right)a^4 = \frac{11}{4}a^4$$

Subtract the triangular area under the chord $OA$ to find the shaded area:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = \text{Area}_{\text{curve}} - \text{Area}_{\text{line}} = \frac{11}{4}a^4 - 2a^4 = \frac{3}{4}a^4$$
Thus, the area is $ka^4$ with fraction $k = \frac{3}{4}$.

ai_rubric.Area Between Curve and Line: Integrates curve to $\frac{x^4}{4} - 2ax^3 + \frac{9a^2 x^2}{2}$ (M1, B2). Evaluates limits to get $\frac{11}{4}a^4$ (M1). Calculates $y_A = 4a^3$ and line area $2a^4$ (B1, M1). Shows shaded area $\frac{3}{4}a^4$ (A1).
